name: Tesseract OCR
description: LSTM line-recognition OCR engine for 100+ languages, with CLI and libtesseract C/C++ API; outputs text, hOCR, ALTO, TSV and searchable PDF, and is trainable for new scripts.
journalism_use_case: Baseline fully offline OCR for scanned court filings, FOIA releases and paper archives; the engine under OCRmyPDF, Tika, ICIJ extract and Datashare.
model_licence: Apache-2.0 for tessdata traineddata from the same project (verify per language pack)
deployment: local CLI/library; distro packages, Homebrew, Docker; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-15, archived=false, 77,536 stars; release 5.5.4 published 2026-10-28
external_deps: Leptonica; optional language traineddata downloads
data_flows: fully local, no network at inference
limitations: weak on handwriting and badly degraded scans; no layout or table-structure output beyond hOCR boxes

name: OCRmyPDF
description: Adds an invisible searchable text layer to existing scanned PDFs without re-rendering page images; supports PDF/A output, deskew, clean, rotate and optimise. Wraps Tesseract and Ghostscript.
journalism_use_case: The standard first pass on a scan dump: makes thousands of image-only PDFs grep-able and ingestable by DocumentCloud/OpenAleph while preserving original page images as evidence.
deployment: local CLI; apt/dnf/brew/pip/Docker; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 35,330 stars; release v17.14.2 published 2026-11-16
external_deps: Tesseract 4.1.1+, Ghostscript, optional jbig2enc/unpaper
data_flows: fully local
limitations: inherits Tesseract's accuracy ceiling; produces a PDF, not structured data; no table extraction

name: PaddleOCR / PP-StructureV3
description: OCR and document-parsing toolkit: PP-OCRv5 does detection plus recognition across ~50 languages; PP-StructureV3 converts complex PDFs and images to Markdown/JSON with layout regions, coordinates and table structure.
journalism_use_case: Strongest open option for Chinese, Arabic and Cyrillic document sets, and for turning scanned reports with tables into structured output on self-hosted hardware.
model_licence: not verified — code is Apache-2.0 but per-model weights are distributed via HuggingFace/ModelScope and were not individually confirmed
deployment: local pip/Docker; CPU or NVIDIA GPU; tiered model sizes
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-09-16, archived=false, 92,754 stars; release v3.7.0 published 2026-06-11
external_deps: PaddlePaddle runtime; first-run weight download
data_flows: local inference; first run fetches weights from HuggingFace/ModelScope (can be pre-staged offline)
limitations: PaddlePaddle dependency is heavier and less familiar than PyTorch; weights licensing unconfirmed, so commercial/redistribution status needs per-model checking

name: Kraken
description: OCR/HTR system for historical and handwritten material: baseline segmentation, trainable recognition models, right-to-left and bidirectional script support, ALTO/PageXML output. The recognition engine behind eScriptorium.
journalism_use_case: The practical open engine for archival investigations — handwritten registers, ledgers, colonial-era records — where a model can be fine-tuned on a few hundred transcribed lines of the specific hand.
model_licence: varies by model — public models published on Zenodo with per-model terms; not verified individually
deployment: local pip/conda CLI; GPU strongly advised for training
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-10, archived=false, 1,105 stars; release 7.1 published 2026-08-05
external_deps: PyTorch; Zenodo model downloads
data_flows: local; optional model fetch from Zenodo
limitations: steep learning curve; accuracy on an unseen hand usually requires fine-tuning with manually transcribed ground truth

name: eScriptorium
description: Self-hostable web platform for recognising handwritten documents: upload images, run segmentation and Kraken-based HTR, correct transcriptions collaboratively in the browser, train models, export ALTO/PageXML/text.
journalism_use_case: Gives a non-engineer team a shared interface over a scanned handwritten archive; reporters' corrections become training data that improves recognition across the rest of the collection.
deployment: self-hosted Docker Compose; GPU recommended for training
activity_evidence: GitLab project page fetched 2026-11-16: ~3,508 commits, active develop branch, 6 releases and 215 tags; not archived
external_deps: Kraken, PostgreSQL, Redis
data_flows: fully self-hosted; documents stay on your server
limitations: non-trivial sysadmin burden; hosted on GitLab rather than GitHub; throughput bounded by your own GPU

name: Surya
description: Document-intelligence model doing text recognition, layout analysis, reading order, table-to-HTML with colspan/rowspan, and equation recognition across 90+ languages.
journalism_use_case: High-accuracy local alternative to commercial document AI for messy multi-column reports, forms and financial tables, without sending documents to a vendor.
model_licence: OpenRAIL-M (README licence badge labels 'Model License: OpenRAIL-M' and links to datalab.to/pricing) — not OSI-approved; commercial thresholds apply
deployment: local; NVIDIA GPU via vLLM, or CPU/Apple Silicon via llama.cpp/MLX
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-13, archived=false, 21,594 stars; release v0.24.0 published 2026-11-13; LICENSE file read directly is plain Apache-2.0 (code only)
external_deps: vLLM or llama.cpp/mlx_vlm server; HuggingFace weight download
data_flows: local inference; the auto-spawned inference server can be pointed at a remote OpenAI-compatible endpoint — an exfiltration risk to configure carefully
limitations: code is Apache-2.0 but the weights are NOT open source; the revenue/funding threshold can bind larger publishers; GPU needed for real throughput

name: Marker
description: Converts PDF, image, PPTX, DOCX, XLSX, HTML and EPUB to Markdown, JSON, HTML or chunked output, preserving tables, forms, equations, links and references, extracting images and stripping headers/footers.
journalism_use_case: Workhorse for turning a heterogeneous leak (mixed PDFs, Office files, scans) into clean Markdown that is searchable and diffable, with page-level traceability.
model_licence: OpenRAIL-M for the Surya/Datalab weights it uses (README badge 'Model License: OpenRAIL-M' linking to datalab.to/pricing) — commercial thresholds apply
deployment: local pip/Docker; NVIDIA GPU via vLLM, or CPU/Apple Silicon via llama.cpp
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-14, archived=false, 40,935 stars; release v2.2.0 published 2026-11-12; LICENSE read directly is plain Apache-2.0
external_deps: Surya models; vLLM or llama.cpp; optional third-party LLM API for enhancement mode
data_flows: local by default; the optional LLM-enhancement mode sends page content to an external provider and must stay off for confidential material
limitations: weights-licence threshold binds large newsrooms; the accuracy-boosting LLM mode is incompatible with source protection unless pointed at a self-hosted model

name: Docling
maintainer: docling-project (originated at IBM Research; now LF AI & Data)
description: Parses PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, images and audio into a unified DoclingDocument with page layout understanding, table-structure recognition and reading order; exports Markdown, HTML, JSON, DocTags.
journalism_use_case: Permissively licensed, fully local parser for sensitive leaks where even model-weight restrictions are unacceptable; the unified document model suits repeatable newsroom ingest pipelines.
model_licence: not verified individually — layout and TableFormer models distributed via HuggingFace under docling-project; per-model terms not confirmed
deployment: local pip/CLI/Docker; CPU-capable, GPU optional
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 70,640 stars; release v2.150.1 published 2026-11-14
external_deps: HuggingFace model downloads; optional Tesseract/EasyOCR/RapidOCR backends; optional VLM pipelines
data_flows: local; first-run model download from HuggingFace; optional remote VLM backends send content out if enabled
limitations: very fast release cadence means API churn; OCR quality depends on the plugged-in backend engine

name: olmOCR
description: Toolkit plus fine-tuned vision-language models that linearise PDFs and document images into clean text/Markdown, preserving reading order across columns, tables and equations; ships olmOCR-bench.
journalism_use_case: Genuinely open-weights VLM OCR — rare in this category — so a newsroom can run state-of-the-art document linearisation on its own GPU with no licence threshold and no vendor seeing the documents.
model_licence: Apache-2.0 (HuggingFace card allenai/olmOCR-2-7B-1025); fine-tuned from Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct so Qwen's terms also apply; AI2 frames use under its Responsible Use Guidelines
deployment: local GPU inference; 7B model, FP8 quantised variant recommended
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-03-25, archived=false, 19,824 stars; release v0.4.27 published 2026-03-12 — roughly eight months without a push
external_deps: NVIDIA GPU, vLLM/SGLang, Poppler; HuggingFace weights
data_flows: local inference once weights are downloaded
limitations: no repo activity since March 2026 — treat the current release as a snapshot; needs a sizeable NVIDIA GPU, not laptop-friendly

name: Apache Tika
description: Content analysis toolkit detecting and extracting text and metadata from over a thousand file types via one interface, with optional Tesseract-backed OCR, a REST server mode and forked-parser isolation for untrusted input.
journalism_use_case: The format-coverage backbone of leak processing — one API over PDFs, legacy Office, email, archives and images, plus metadata (authors, timestamps, software) that is often the story. Underpins ICIJ extract, Datashare and OpenAleph.
deployment: local JAR/CLI, tika-server REST, Docker; Python and other clients
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 4,150 stars; no GitHub release object (ASF publishes via Apache dist)
external_deps: optional Tesseract for OCR; many format-specific libraries
data_flows: fully local
limitations: extraction only — no layout model, table structure or reading-order reconstruction; parsing untrusted files in-process is a security risk, so sandbox tika-server; JVM overhead

name: Camelot
maintainer: camelot-dev community (fork of the archived atlanhq/camelot)
description: Extracts tables from text-based PDFs using 'lattice' (ruling-line) and 'stream' (whitespace) strategies, returning pandas DataFrames with per-table accuracy and whitespace quality metrics; exports CSV/JSON/Excel/SQLite.
journalism_use_case: Pulling budget tables, campaign-finance schedules and procurement annexes out of born-digital PDFs into spreadsheets; the per-table accuracy score tells a reporter which extractions need manual checking.
deployment: local pip; Ghostscript needed for the lattice backend
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 3,857 stars; release v2.0.0 published 2026-06-04. The original atlanhq/camelot is archived=true, last push 2023-01
external_deps: Ghostscript, pdfminer.six, OpenCV, pandas
data_flows: fully local
limitations: needs a real text layer — scans must be OCR'd first; struggles with merged cells, multi-page spanning tables and rotated pages; the widely-linked atlanhq repo is dead

name: pdfplumber
description: Exposes per-character, per-word and per-line geometry from PDFs plus table detection and cropping, with visual debugging that renders detected objects over the page image.
journalism_use_case: Built by a data journalist and widely used in newsrooms: character-level coordinates let you reconstruct layout-dependent documents (disclosure forms, tabular filings) exactly, and the visual debugger makes an extraction auditable.
deployment: local pip; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-10-15, archived=false, 10,904 stars; release v0.11.10 published 2026-06-15
external_deps: pdfminer.six; Pillow/ImageMagick for visual debugging
data_flows: fully local
limitations: no OCR — text-layer PDFs only; table detection needs per-document strategy tuning; slow on very large files

name: Tabula
maintainer: Tabula (created by journalists via OpenNews/ProPublica/La Nación lineage)
description: Desktop GUI (with tabula-java and tabula-py library siblings) for selecting and liberating data tables trapped inside PDF files, exporting CSV, TSV or JSON.
journalism_use_case: The canonical no-code newsroom tool: a reporter draws a box around a table in a PDF budget or disclosure filing and gets a CSV, with no engineer and no cloud service involved.
language_stack: Ruby/JavaScript GUI over Java (tabula-java); Python wrapper tabula-py
deployment: local desktop app (macOS/Windows/Linux), runs a local web UI; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2025-03-14, archived=false, 7,496 stars — slow-moving but not archived; the tabula-java engine is maintained separately
external_deps: Java runtime
data_flows: fully local — the UI is served from localhost, nothing uploaded
limitations: text-layer PDFs only (no OCR); manual selection does not scale to thousands of documents; GUI development has largely stalled in favour of the libraries

name: PyMuPDF
description: Fast Python bindings to MuPDF for text and image extraction, page rendering to raster, annotation and true redaction, document assembly and conversion across PDF, XPS, EPUB and images.
journalism_use_case: Fastest route to rasterising pages for OCR, and to applying genuine redactions that remove the underlying text rather than drawing a black box over it — a real newsroom failure mode it prevents.
licence: AGPL-3.0 (dual-licensed; Artifex sells a commercial licence)
deployment: local pip wheels; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-15, archived=false, 11,143 stars; release 2.1 published 2026-11-02
external_deps: bundled MuPDF
data_flows: fully local
limitations: AGPL-3.0 is the key caveat — embedding it in a network-facing newsroom service triggers source-release obligations unless you buy Artifex's commercial licence; pypdf (BSD-style) or pdfminer.six are the permissive alternatives

name: Whisper
description: Reference PyTorch implementation and weights for the Whisper encoder-decoder ASR model, covering transcription and translation across roughly 99 languages.
journalism_use_case: Baseline transcription of interviews and leaked audio where model provenance matters; the canonical implementation that nearly every newsroom transcription tool wraps.
deployment: local CLI/library; CPU or CUDA GPU
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-08-31, archived=false, 112,825 stars; upstream moves slowly while forks move faster
external_deps: PyTorch, ffmpeg; weights downloaded on first run
data_flows: fully local inference after weight download; no audio leaves the machine
limitations: no speaker diarisation; approximate word timestamps; large-v3 needs roughly 10GB VRAM; prone to hallucinated text on silence and poor recordings

name: whisper.cpp
description: Plain C/C++ port of Whisper inference on the ggml tensor library, with quantised models, CoreML/Metal/CUDA/Vulkan backends, and a bundled CLI and server.
journalism_use_case: Air-gapped transcription of sensitive source audio on a laptop with no GPU and no network; the engine inside many desktop newsroom transcription apps.
deployment: local binary/library; CPU, Apple Silicon Metal/CoreML, CUDA, Vulkan; mobile and embedded targets
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 55,238 stars; release v1.9.5 published 2026-10-06
external_deps: ffmpeg for format conversion; optional backend SDKs
data_flows: fully local; model files fetched once
limitations: no built-in diarisation; quantisation trades accuracy for speed; API churn across releases can break downstream wrappers

name: faster-whisper
description: Whisper reimplementation on CTranslate2 delivering large speed and memory gains over the reference model, with integrated VAD filtering and batched inference.
journalism_use_case: Bulk processing of large audio archives — press-conference backlogs, months of broadcast — where throughput per GPU-hour decides whether the investigation is affordable.
deployment: local Python library; CPU with int8 or CUDA GPU with float16
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-12, archived=false, 26,790 stars; release v1.2.1 published 2025-10-31
external_deps: CTranslate2, cuDNN/cuBLAS for GPU, Silero VAD, HuggingFace Hub for weights
data_flows: local inference; weights pulled from HuggingFace on first use
limitations: no diarisation; the latest tag predates a year of commits, so pinning to a release loses fixes; CUDA library version mismatches are a common install failure

name: WhisperX
description: Pipeline combining faster-whisper transcription with wav2vec2 forced alignment for accurate word-level timestamps and optional pyannote speaker diarisation.
journalism_use_case: Producing quote-accurate, speaker-attributed transcripts of multi-party interviews and hearings, where you must jump to the exact second a phrase was spoken to verify it.
model_licence: mixed — Whisper MIT; wav2vec2 aligners vary by language; pyannote diarisation weights MIT but gated on HuggingFace
deployment: local CLI and Python API; CUDA GPU strongly preferred
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-12, archived=false, 25,364 stars; release v3.8.6 published 2026-05-25
external_deps: faster-whisper, pyannote.audio, torchaudio, ffmpeg; HuggingFace token for gated diarisation models
data_flows: local inference, but obtaining diarisation weights requires accepting pyannote's HuggingFace gate, which discloses your HF identity to the model authors
limitations: diarisation degrades on overlapping speech and phone audio; alignment-model coverage is uneven outside major languages; heavy dependency stack; ~10GB VRAM for large-v3 plus diarisation

name: pyannote.audio
description: PyTorch toolkit of neural building blocks for speaker diarisation: voice activity detection, speaker change and overlap detection, embeddings, and end-to-end pretrained pipelines.
journalism_use_case: The de facto open diarisation layer for newsroom pipelines — separating who spoke when in interviews, conference calls and intercepted audio before transcription.
model_licence: MIT but GATED — the speaker-diarization-3.1 card states 'You need to agree to share your Hugging Face information to access this model'; it also states the pipeline 'will always remain open-source'
deployment: local Python library; CPU usable, CUDA GPU much faster; the maintainer also sells a hosted pyannote.ai API
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 10,804 stars; release 4.0.7 published 2026-06-30; homepage set to pyannote.ai
external_deps: torch, torchaudio, HuggingFace Hub; HF account and token for gated pipelines
data_flows: inference is local, but the gate means model authors learn your HuggingFace identity at download time; the commercial pyannote.ai service is separate and would send audio off-machine
limitations: gating is a real blocker for air-gapped or anonymity-sensitive work — pre-fetch weights; accuracy drops on overlapping speech, telephone-band audio and many speakers; increasingly coupled to a commercial offering

name: NVIDIA NeMo Speech
description: NVIDIA's speech AI framework for training and running ASR, diarisation and TTS; home of the Parakeet and Canary ASR families and the Sortformer/MSDD diarisation models.
journalism_use_case: High-accuracy English transcription and diarisation at archive scale, and the most realistic route to fine-tuning an ASR model on a dialect or jargon a specific investigation requires.
model_licence: VARIES AND MATTERS — nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 is CC-BY-4.0 (commercial use allowed); nvidia/diar_sortformer_4spk-v1 is CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial only), both read off the HF cards 2026-11-16
deployment: self-hosted; NVIDIA GPU effectively required; container images provided
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 18,758 stars; release v3.0.0 published 2026-08-07; the github.com/NVIDIA/NeMo path now resolves to NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech
external_deps: PyTorch, CUDA, HuggingFace Hub / NVIDIA NGC for checkpoints
data_flows: local inference and training; checkpoints downloaded from NGC/HuggingFace
limitations: the CC-BY-NC-4.0 licence on Sortformer diarisation weights bars use in commercially published journalism unless separately licensed or substituted; NVIDIA-GPU-centric; the repo was reorganised so older tutorials and import paths are stale

name: sherpa-onnx
description: Next-gen Kaldi runtime doing speech-to-text, speaker diarisation, VAD, speech enhancement and TTS via onnxruntime with no internet connection, exposed through a dozen language bindings.
journalism_use_case: Transcription on locked-down or offline hardware — field laptops, phones, Raspberry Pi — for hostile-environment reporting where sending audio to any server is unacceptable.
model_licence: varies per exported checkpoint (Whisper, Zipformer, Paraformer and others distributed separately) — verify the specific model
language_stack: C++ core with Python, C, Java, C#, Go, Swift, Kotlin, JS bindings
deployment: local/embedded; CPU-only viable; Android, iOS, Raspberry Pi, RISC-V, x86_64 servers, websocket server/client
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 15,983 stars; release v2.0.1 published 2026-10-26
external_deps: onnxruntime; pre-exported model archives from the project's release pages
data_flows: explicitly designed for no-internet operation; nothing leaves the device
limitations: model-zoo quality varies widely by language; diarisation is simpler than pyannote/Sortformer; sprawling documentation and you must match model and runtime versions

name: Buzz
description: Cross-platform desktop GUI that transcribes and translates audio offline using Whisper, with live recording, batch queues and SRT/VTT/TXT export.
journalism_use_case: The practical default for a reporter with no command line: drag an interview recording in, get a timestamped transcript and subtitles without the file leaving the laptop.
model_licence: MIT (Whisper / whisper.cpp / faster-whisper weights); the optional OpenAI API mode uses a hosted model instead
deployment: desktop app for macOS, Windows, Linux; CPU workable, GPU optional
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 22,844 stars; release v1.4.5 published 2026-08-23
external_deps: ffmpeg, whisper.cpp/faster-whisper backends; optional OpenAI API key
data_flows: local by default, but Buzz also offers an OpenAI Whisper API backend — selecting it uploads audio to OpenAI and must be avoided for confidential source material
limitations: diarisation is not a first-class feature; large models are slow on CPU; the optional cloud backend is a foot-gun that should be disabled by newsroom policy

name: noScribe
description: Desktop GUI wrapping Whisper and pyannote for automated interview transcription with speaker identification, plus an integrated editor for correcting machine output against the audio.
journalism_use_case: Purpose-built for the investigative workflow: long qualitative interviews, speaker-labelled transcripts, and a correction editor so every published quote has been human-verified.
model_licence: Whisper MIT; pyannote diarisation weights MIT but gated on HuggingFace
deployment: desktop app for Windows, macOS, Linux; CPU, GPU optional
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-09, archived=false, 2,248 stars; release v0.8 published 2026-10-06
external_deps: Whisper/faster-whisper, pyannote.audio, ffmpeg
data_flows: local processing; model weights downloaded once (pyannote gate applies)
limitations: CPU transcription of a long interview takes hours; GPL-3.0 constrains embedding in proprietary newsroom systems; single-maintainer project; pre-fetch gated weights before going offline

name: Subtitle Edit
description: Mature subtitle editor supporting around 300 subtitle formats, with waveform and spectrogram views, synchronisation, OCR of hardcoded subtitles and built-in Whisper-based audio-to-text.
journalism_use_case: Turning raw transcripts into broadcast-ready captions, and precisely re-timing or verifying subtitles on leaked or downloaded video evidence against the waveform.
model_licence: n/a for the editor; bundled Whisper backends use MIT weights
deployment: desktop app, primarily Windows (Linux/macOS via mono/wine); CPU
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 15,015 stars; release v5.4.0 published 2026-11-06
external_deps: ffmpeg, optional Whisper engines, optional Tesseract for subtitle OCR
data_flows: local by default; optional machine-translation features call third-party services and would send subtitle text off-machine
limitations: Windows-centric; online translation must be switched off for sensitive material; dense UI aimed at subtitlers rather than reporters

name: Montreal Forced Aligner
description: Command-line forced aligner built on Kaldi that aligns an existing transcript to audio at word and phone level using trained acoustic models and pronunciation dictionaries.
journalism_use_case: Authenticating or precisely timestamping a known transcript against a recording — essential when you must show a specific phrase occurs at a specific moment in leaked audio.
model_licence: pretrained acoustic models and dictionaries distributed separately per language — verify each
deployment: local CLI via conda; CPU-based, no GPU required
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-15, archived=false, 1,918 stars; release v3.4.3 published 2026-10-08
external_deps: Kaldi, PostgreSQL for the corpus database, conda, language-specific acoustic models and dictionaries
data_flows: fully local; model and dictionary downloads from the project index
limitations: aligns, does not recognise — you must supply a transcript; needs a pronunciation dictionary for the language; conda-only install plus PostgreSQL is awkward; out-of-dictionary proper names (common in investigations) align poorly

name: Hyperaudio Lite
description: Very lightweight vanilla-JavaScript interactive transcript player that syncs a timed transcript with audio or video: clicking any word seeks the media and the active word highlights during playback.
journalism_use_case: Publishing the evidence alongside the story — an embeddable, searchable, clickable transcript of an interview or hearing that lets readers verify a quote in its original audio context.
deployment: client-side browser library, static hosting; no server or GPU
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-10-30, archived=false, 183 stars; release v2.6.6 published 2026-09-21
external_deps: none required; consumes transcript HTML/WebVTT from an upstream ASR tool
data_flows: entirely client-side; whatever you publish is public by design
limitations: presentation layer only — the timed transcript must be generated elsewhere; small niche project; accessibility and styling are left to the implementer

name: LibreTranslate
description: Self-hostable machine translation API and web UI wrapping Argos Translate models; translates text, HTML and uploaded documents with language auto-detection, API keys and rate limiting.
journalism_use_case: A newsroom-run translation endpoint for leaked documents so no text leaves the organisation; can be called by OpenAleph/Datashare-style pipelines for bulk gisting of foreign-language material.
model_licence: inherits Argos Translate model packages (largely open, derived from OPUS/OPUS-MT data; verify per language pair)
language_stack: Python (Flask) + JS; Argos Translate and CTranslate2 backend
deployment: self-hosted Docker/pip, CPU-only workable, optional CUDA; a paid hosted instance also exists
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-14, archived=false, 17,771 stars; release v1.9.6 published 2026-05-26
external_deps: argostranslate, ctranslate2, sentencepiece, stanza; downloads model packages on first run
data_flows: fully local when self-hosted; the public libretranslate.com API sends text to a third party and must be avoided for leaks
limitations: quality well below commercial MT on low-resource pairs; AGPL-3.0 network copyleft applies if you expose a modified instance; no translation memory or human-review workflow

name: Argos Translate
description: Offline neural MT library and CLI with installable per-language-pair model packages built on CTranslate2, SentencePiece and Stanza; supports pivot translation through English where no direct model exists.
journalism_use_case: Air-gapped batch translation of document dumps from a laptop or evidence machine; the Python API makes it easy to script translation of thousands of files with no network call.
model_licence: per-package, mostly open (derived from OPUS/OPUS-MT data) — verify the individual .argosmodel package
deployment: pip/Docker, local CPU inference, GPU optional
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-14, archived=false, 6,657 stars; GitHub release tag v1.4.0 dated 2021-08-24 — the releases page is stale while commits continue and PyPI is the live channel
external_deps: ctranslate2, sentencepiece, stanza; Argos package index for model download
data_flows: none at inference once models are downloaded; model download hits the Argos package index
limitations: narrower language coverage than NLLB/MADLAD; pivoting through English compounds errors; plain text/HTML only, no document-format preservation

name: CTranslate2
description: Fast C++/Python inference engine for Transformer models with converters for OpenNMT, Fairseq, Marian, OPUS-MT and HuggingFace Transformers; README documents support for M2M-100, NLLB, mBART, MADLAD-400 and Whisper with FP16/BF16/INT16/INT8 and AWQ INT4 quantisation.
journalism_use_case: The engine that makes offline MT and Whisper transcription practical on newsroom hardware — int8 quantisation lets a 600M-1.3B translation model run on a CPU laptop instead of a cloud API.
model_licence: n/a (engine only; converted weights keep their own licences)
deployment: pip wheel/Docker/embed; CPU (x86-64, ARM64) or CUDA/ROCm GPU
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-10, archived=false, 4,753 stars; release v4.9.0 published 2026-11-10
external_deps: oneDNN/OpenBLAS, optional CUDA/cuDNN; conversion needs the source framework
data_flows: entirely local
limitations: engineer-facing — no UI, no file handling, you supply and convert the model; quantisation costs some quality; memory scales with model size

name: Helsinki-NLP OPUS-MT
maintainer: Language Technology Research Group, University of Helsinki
description: Large open model zoo of Marian-trained bilingual and multilingual MT models covering hundreds of language pairs, distributed via the Opus-MT repo, OPUS-MT-train recipes and Helsinki-NLP/* HuggingFace checkpoints usable with MarianMT or CTranslate2.
journalism_use_case: The default open weights for cross-border reporting — translate Russian, Ukrainian, Arabic, Turkish, Chinese or Balkan-language documents locally, with a permissive weights licence that allows commercial publication.
model_licence: CC-BY-4.0 verified on the HuggingFace card for Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-ru-en — check each pair, coverage varies
language_stack: Python service code, Makefile training pipelines; Marian/CTranslate2 inference
deployment: local inference via transformers or CTranslate2/Argos packaging; CPU-feasible (models are ~75-300M params)
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: Opus-MT pushed_at 2026-02-23, archived=false, 876 stars; OPUS-MT-train also active and not archived
external_deps: HuggingFace hub or OPUS-MT downloads, sentencepiece
data_flows: local after download; HF hub fetch on first use
limitations: bilingual models mean many files to manage; quality varies sharply by pair; older pairs were trained on pre-2020 OPUS data and are weak on slang, OCR noise and code-switching

name: GlotLID
description: FastText-based language identification aimed at low-resource languages; the stable v4 model covers roughly 2,060 labels built from 1,902 ISO-639-3 codes with script distinctions, shipped as model.bin plus a faster small variant.
journalism_use_case: Identifies the languages fastText's lid.176 silently misses — minority and diaspora languages in document dumps — and because labels carry script codes it distinguishes e.g. Serbian in Cyrillic from Serbian in Latin.
licence: Apache-2.0 with additional notices — the LICENSE file read directly opens 'Apache License 2.0 plus notices' and appends a notice on training data and model behaviour (GitHub API reports NOASSERTION)
model_licence: Apache-2.0 with the same additional notices
deployment: pip plus a local model file; CPU-only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-09, archived=false, 228 stars; no GitHub releases — versioning happens via model files on HuggingFace
external_deps: fasttext wheel, HuggingFace hub for the model file
data_flows: local after model download
limitations: no tagged releases and research-project cadence; thousands of labels mean many confusable low-confidence classes, so thresholding is essential; appended notices warn about training-data provenance

name: uroman
maintainer: Ulf Hermjakob, USC Information Sciences Institute
description: Universal romaniser converting text in essentially any script to the Latin alphabet without knowing the language, driven by Unicode data plus language-specific rule tables; available as a Perl script and a Python package.
journalism_use_case: Makes non-Latin-script corpora searchable and joinable — romanise Arabic, Cyrillic, Devanagari, Thai or Chinese names so a sanctions list, corporate registry and leaked ledger can be fuzzy-matched in one Latin-script index.
licence: MIT-style permissive with an added acknowledgement condition — LICENSE.txt read directly grants MIT-equivalent rights but states 'Any publication of projects using uroman shall acknowledge its use'; not a clean SPDX id (GitHub API reports NOASSERTION)
deployment: local CLI or pip library; CPU-only, negligible resources
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2024-07-26, archived=false, 257 stars; latest release v1.3.1 published 2024-06-28 — dormant since mid-2024
external_deps: none significant
data_flows: entirely local
limitations: romanisation is lossy and irreversible; output follows no single standard scheme (not ALA-LC or BGN/PCGN), so it is a matching aid rather than a citable rendering; the acknowledgement clause is a non-standard condition to track

name: sentence-transformers (with LaBSE / multilingual-e5)
description: Framework for sentence, paragraph and image embeddings; with multilingual checkpoints such as LaBSE (109 languages) or multilingual-e5-large it maps text from different languages into one shared vector space for cross-language semantic search and parallel-sentence mining.
journalism_use_case: Query a multilingual leak in your own language and retrieve semantically matching passages in others; also used to align a translation against its original and find near-duplicate documents across language editions.
model_licence: Apache-2.0 for sentence-transformers/LaBSE; MIT for intfloat/multilingual-e5-large (both read off their HuggingFace cards)
deployment: pip, local; CPU workable for modest corpora, GPU for bulk encoding
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 19,286 stars; release v6.3.0 published 2026-11-11. Note the UKPLab/sentence-transformers URL now redirects to huggingface/sentence-transformers
external_deps: transformers, torch, HuggingFace hub; optional faiss or a vector DB
data_flows: local after model download; pre-stage weights for air-gapped work
limitations: embedding quality degrades for low-resource languages; returns passages not translations, so an MT or human step is still needed; you must build the index, storage and UI around it

name: spaCy
description: Industrial-strength Python NLP library with trained pipelines for tokenisation, POS, dependency parsing and named-entity recognition across roughly 25 languages, plus a rule-based Matcher/EntityRuler and a plugin architecture.
journalism_use_case: Baseline workhorse for pulling person, organisation, location and money mentions out of leaked documents and mailboxes; EntityRuler lets reporters add gazetteers of target names before a full NER pass.
model_licence: varies by pipeline package (en_core_web_* are MIT; some non-English packages carry corpus-derived terms) — not verified individually
deployment: pip, fully local; CPU sufficient for small/medium pipelines, GPU optional for transformer pipelines
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-10-27, archived=false, 34,061 stars; release release-v3.8.18 published 2026-10-26
external_deps: thinc, numpy; model packages downloaded on first use
data_flows: local-only inference; only model download touches the network
limitations: statistical NER degrades on OCR-noisy leak text, unusual transliterations and non-Latin scripts; no entity linking to real-world identifiers out of the box; fixed label set unless retrained

name: GLiNER
description: Generalist lightweight NER model that extracts arbitrary user-specified entity types at inference time by passing type names as prompts, using a bidirectional encoder rather than an autoregressive LLM.
journalism_use_case: Define bespoke labels for an investigation — 'shell company', 'vessel', 'bank account', 'politically exposed person' — and sweep a leak without annotating training data or sending documents to an API.
model_licence: SPLIT — v2.1 checkpoints (urchade/gliner_small-v2.1, urchade/gliner_multi-v2.1) are apache-2.0, while the older v0/v1 checkpoints (urchade/gliner_base, gliner_multi, gliner_small/medium/large-v1) are cc-by-nc-4.0, research only
deployment: pip, local inference; CPU for small models, GPU for large/multi models and bulk corpora
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-11, archived=false, 4,266 stars; release v0.2.30 published 2026-11-02
external_deps: transformers, torch; checkpoints from HuggingFace Hub
data_flows: local inference after model download; no text leaves the machine
limitations: licence trap — the older, still widely cited v0/v1 weights are CC-BY-NC and unusable by commercial newsrooms; prompt-sensitive recall; long documents must be chunked; no linking or deduplication of extracted spans

name: Presidio
maintainer: data-privacy-stack (project moved out of the microsoft org; github.com/microsoft/presidio now redirects)
description: Modular PII detection and anonymisation framework combining regex/checksum recognisers, NER models (spaCy, Stanza, transformers) and context enhancement, with separate analyzer, anonymizer, image-redactor and structured-data packages.
journalism_use_case: Works in both directions — find names, national IDs, IBANs and phone numbers inside a leak, and redact them before publishing documents or sharing a corpus with partner outlets.
model_licence: n/a (NER backends carry their own model licences)
deployment: pip packages or Docker services, fully self-hosted; CPU fine unless a transformer recogniser is used
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: full_name resolves to data-privacy-stack/presidio, pushed_at 2026-11-14, archived=false, 11,896 stars; release 2.2.366 published 2026-10-27
external_deps: spaCy/Stanza/transformers NER engines; optional Tesseract for image redaction
data_flows: local by default; optional LLM-based recognisers would send text to a third party if configured
limitations: recall on unusual name forms and non-English entities depends entirely on the chosen NER backend; governance recently changed hands so pin versions; redaction is best-effort and needs human review before publication

name: Stanza
description: Stanford's Python NLP toolkit with neural pipelines for tokenisation, lemmatisation, POS, dependency parsing and NER in 70+ languages, plus a client for the Java CoreNLP server.
journalism_use_case: Entity extraction from non-English leaks — Russian, Arabic, Ukrainian, Chinese registries and correspondence — where English-first pipelines fail; also the bridge to CoreNLP's SUTime and OpenIE.
licence: Apache-2.0 — GitHub licence detection reports 'Other' but the LICENSE file read directly is the Apache License 2.0 (Copyright 2019 Board of Trustees of Leland Stanford Junior University)
model_licence: not verified — the Available Models documentation page states no licence for the downloadable model archives, and training treebanks/NER corpora may carry their own restrictions
deployment: pip, local; CPU usable, GPU much faster for bulk work
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-15, archived=false, 7,917 stars; release v1.15.1 published 2026-11-14
external_deps: torch; model archives downloaded from Stanford/HuggingFace
data_flows: local inference; model download only
limitations: model licensing is the open question — code is Apache-2.0 but per-language weights derive from corpora with their own terms; NER label sets vary by language, so cross-language merging needs mapping

name: entity-fishing
description: Machine-learning service that recognises and disambiguates mentions in text and PDFs against Wikidata and Wikipedia, exposed as a self-hosted REST API, with support for English, French, German, Spanish and Italian among others.
journalism_use_case: Resolve ambiguous names in documents to stable Wikidata QIDs so the same politician or company spelled three ways across a leak collapses into one node.
model_licence: n/a (ships its own models and knowledge-base builds)
deployment: self-hosted service or Docker; requires a locally built Wikidata/Wikipedia knowledge base of tens of GB — the main setup cost
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-08-05, archived=false, 270 stars; no GitHub release objects (most recent tag 0.0.6)
external_deps: JVM; LMDB-backed knowledge base derived from Wikidata/Wikipedia dumps
data_flows: fully local once the knowledge base is built — a genuine advantage over hosted linking APIs for sensitive leaks
limitations: heavy install and large disk footprint; the knowledge base goes stale unless rebuilt; coverage limited to entities that exist in Wikidata, which excludes most shell companies and private individuals in a leak

name: dedupe
maintainer: dedupe.io / Forest Gregg and Derek Eder (dedupeio)
description: Python library for fuzzy matching, deduplication and entity resolution that learns blocking predicates and field comparators from interactive human labelling of candidate pairs.
journalism_use_case: The classic newsroom tool for collapsing duplicate rows in a messy registry or donor list; the active-learning console means a reporter, not an engineer, supplies the match/no-match judgements.
deployment: pip, fully local; CPU only, memory-bound on large tables
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2025-07-29, archived=false, 4,530 stars; no GitHub release objects, most recent version tag v3.0.3 — quiet for over a year
external_deps: scikit-learn, numpy; csvdedupe/pandas-dedupe wrappers are separate projects
data_flows: local only; the commercial hosted dedupe.io service is a separate product from this MIT library
limitations: no tagged release since v3.0.3; does not scale comfortably past a few million records; results depend on the labelling session, so two reporters can get different clusters from the same data

name: Splink
maintainer: UK Ministry of Justice Analytical Services
description: Probabilistic data-linkage library implementing the Fellegi-Sunter model with unsupervised EM parameter estimation, SQL-backend execution (DuckDB, Spark, PostgreSQL) and interactive match-weight and cluster visualisations.
journalism_use_case: Link people across two large datasets with no shared key — a sanctions list against a corporate registry, or a leak's client list against a property register — at a scale where dedupe would stall, with auditable per-comparison match weights.
deployment: pip; DuckDB backend runs fully locally on a laptop for millions of records, Spark/Athena for 100M+; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-11, archived=false, 2,586 stars; release v5.0.0 published 2026-09-18
external_deps: duckdb by default; optional pyspark, psycopg2
data_flows: local with the DuckDB backend; cloud Spark/Athena backends would move data to that infrastructure
limitations: requires real understanding of blocking rules and m/u probabilities to avoid false links — the output is a probability, not a verdict; v5 broke APIs versus v3/v4 tutorials still circulating; no built-in name normalisation, so pair it with rigour first

name: RapidFuzz
description: Fast C++-backed fuzzy string matching and similarity metrics (Levenshtein, Damerau-Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler, token-set/partial ratios) with a FuzzyWuzzy-compatible API and vectorised cdist matrix scoring.
journalism_use_case: The low-level primitive under most name matching — score a leaked name list against a sanctions or PEP list, or cluster near-identical company names, without fuzzywuzzy's GPL licensing and slowness.
deployment: pip (prebuilt wheels), fully local; CPU only, multithreaded cdist
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-09, archived=false, 4,208 stars
external_deps: none beyond the bundled C++ extension (optional numpy for cdist)
data_flows: local only
limitations: a metric library, not a matching system — no blocking, clustering or threshold guidance; raw edit distance mismatches transliterated and reordered names (Mohammed/Muhammad, surname-first registries), so normalise with rigour before scoring

name: rigour (supersedes fingerprints)
description: Data cleaning and validation functions for the entity-matching domain: name normalisation and fingerprinting, company-type and legal-form expansion, address handling, language/territory codes, and checksum validation for identifiers such as IBAN, LEI and ISIN.
journalism_use_case: The unglamorous preprocessing that decides whether matching works at all — turning 'OOO Rosneft-Trading Ltd.' and 'ROSNEFT TRADING LIMITED' into the same key before any fuzzy scorer sees them.
deployment: pip, fully local; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-07, archived=false, 73 stars. The older alephdata/fingerprints URL now redirects to opensanctions/fingerprints (MIT, pushed 2025-11-24), whose README states the codebase is now included in rigour and that fingerprints is UNMAINTAINED
external_deps: normality, locale data; bundled reference datasets
data_flows: local only
limitations: use rigour, not the widely cited fingerprints package; normalisation rules are tuned for Latin-script corporate and sanctions data and are weaker on CJK and Arabic name forms; small community

name: nomenklatura
description: Framework and CLI for integrating FollowTheMoney entity streams from multiple sources: statement-based entity stores, name and identifier matching algorithms, blocking indexes, human-reviewed deduplication and a persistent resolver graph of merge judgements.
journalism_use_case: The deduplication engine behind OpenSanctions — merge the same oligarch or company across sanctions lists, leaks and registries while keeping an auditable record of every merge a human approved.
deployment: pip plus CLI, local; optional Elasticsearch/OpenSearch index for scale; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 273 stars; release 4.17.3 published 2026-10-21
external_deps: followthemoney, rigour; optional Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, Redis
data_flows: local; enrichment connectors can query external APIs (OpenCorporates, Wikidata) only if explicitly configured
limitations: only speaks FollowTheMoney, so arbitrary CSVs must be mapped into the ontology first — a non-trivial modelling step; docs assume familiarity with the OpenSanctions pipeline; resolver files become artefacts you must version deliberately

name: FollowTheMoney
description: Data model, schema definitions and processing tools for investigative entity data — people, companies, assets, payments, directorships, legal cases — with typed properties, validation, name/identifier type handling and export to graph and tabular formats.
journalism_use_case: The shared vocabulary that makes cross-dataset linking possible: map a leak, a registry and a sanctions list into the same Person/Company/Ownership schema so records can actually be compared. Aleph, OpenAleph, yente and nomenklatura all build on it.
language_stack: Python plus a TypeScript sibling package
deployment: pip, fully local library; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-02-28, archived=false, 309 stars; release v3.8.2 published 2025-03-24
external_deps: rigour, banal; optional networkx for graph export
data_flows: local only
limitations: governance is in flux — the alephdata org is winding down alongside Aleph's sunsetting, so confirm which fork is actively maintained before building on it; it is an ontology, not a tool, and mapping messy sources into it is the real work

name: yente
description: Self-hostable HTTP API for entity search and bulk matching against sanctions, PEP and other FollowTheMoney collections, backed by Elasticsearch/OpenSearch and implementing the Reconciliation Service API so OpenRefine can point at it directly.
journalism_use_case: Screen a leaked client or shareholder list against sanctions and PEP data in bulk on your own infrastructure, then reconcile the same spreadsheet from OpenRefine without the names leaving your network.
deployment: Docker Compose with Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, fully self-hosted; CPU only, moderate RAM for the index
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 184 stars; release v5.5.1 published 2026-10-30
external_deps: Elasticsearch or OpenSearch; OpenSanctions bulk data files loaded at index time
data_flows: queries stay local once indexed — the key privacy win over hosted screening APIs. The index DATA is licensed separately by OpenSanctions (CC-BY-NC with paid commercial tiers)
limitations: code is MIT but the data it exists to serve is non-commercial unless licensed, which directly affects commercial newsrooms; matching returns scored candidates that still need human adjudication; the index must be refreshed to stay current

name: OpenRefine
maintainer: OpenRefine community / Code for Science & Society
description: Desktop power tool for messy tabular data: faceting, GREL transformations, key-collision and nearest-neighbour clustering to merge spelling variants, and a reconciliation framework that matches cell values against external identifier services such as Wikidata.
journalism_use_case: The most accessible tool in this pillar — a reporter with no code can cluster 4,000 variant company names in a leaked spreadsheet down to 900 real entities, then reconcile them to Wikidata or a self-hosted yente instance for stable IDs.
deployment: runs locally as a desktop app serving a browser UI; JVM required; CPU only, memory-bound on very large files
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-13, archived=false, 12,107 stars; release 3.10.1 published 2026-03-04
external_deps: JVM; optional reconciliation service endpoints and extensions
data_flows: cleaning and clustering are local, but RECONCILIATION sends cell values to a third-party web service — for a confidential leak, point reconciliation at a self-hosted service such as yente instead of public Wikidata
limitations: reconciliation is the leak risk in an otherwise offline tool; clustering is heuristic and over-merges distinct entities with similar names; large datasets strain the JVM heap; no probabilistic record linkage between two tables

name: OpenAleph
description: Self-hosted platform that stores large document and structured-data collections and makes them searchable and cross-referenceable using the FollowTheMoney entity model. Actively maintained fork of the sunsetted OCCRP Aleph codebase.
journalism_use_case: The primary live candidate for standing up a searchable archive over a multi-million-document leak for a reporting team, with entity cross-referencing against sanctions lists and registries.
language_stack: Python services, JavaScript frontend, Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL
deployment: self-hosted Docker Compose/Kubernetes; substantial infrastructure; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 156 stars; release 5.4.0 published 2026-11-16 (same day as this survey) — the actively maintained line of the Aleph codebase
external_deps: Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, Redis, openaleph/ingest-file workers, Apache Tika
data_flows: fully local/self-hosted; no third-party calls required for core indexing
limitations: heavy infrastructure footprint; smaller maintainer base than OCCRP-era Aleph; Elasticsearch index sizing is the main scaling cost at multi-million-document scale

name: ingest-file (OpenAleph fork)
description: Ingestors that extract the contents of mixed unstructured documents into structured FollowTheMoney data. Maintained fork of alephdata/ingest-file, which is now archived upstream.
journalism_use_case: The extraction and OCR stage of a leak pipeline — turning heterogeneous attachments, scans, mailboxes and archives into indexable structured records.
deployment: self-hosted Docker worker
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 15 stars; release 5.4.0 published 2026-11-12. Upstream alephdata/ingest-file is archived=true with last push 2025-12-19
external_deps: Apache Tika, Tesseract-class OCR, LibreOffice-family converters
data_flows: local processing in worker containers
limitations: AGPL copyleft affects redistribution of modified services; OCR throughput is the usual bottleneck on scanned corpora; very small contributor base

name: ICIJ Datashare
description: Open-source self-hosted document search and analysis platform: ingests PDFs, email, spreadsheets, images and archives, extracts text with OCR on scans, runs named-entity extraction, and indexes everything into Elasticsearch with tagging and recommendations.
journalism_use_case: The reference end-to-end newsroom stack for a leaked document set — a reporter-facing UI over OCR plus entity extraction, deployable as a desktop app for one journalist or in server mode for a cross-border team sharing tags.
model_licence: n/a for the platform; bundled NER models carry their own terms (not verified)
deployment: local desktop distribution or Docker Compose server mode (PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, Redis)
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 783 stars; release 21.24.1 published 2026-11-12 — one of the most actively maintained newsroom platforms in this catalogue
external_deps: Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, Redis; Tika/Tesseract extraction path; NER pipelines include CoreNLP, Ixa Pipes, MITIE and Apache OpenNLP
data_flows: runs on your own machines; the README states no external cloud services are required and sensitive material stays under your control
limitations: server mode needs real infrastructure and ops capacity; AGPL-3.0 obligations if you modify and host it for others; entity types are limited to person/organisation/location, so it indexes rather than resolves; bundled NER engines are older generation

name: ICIJ extract
description: Command-line utility for parallelised content and metadata extraction from heterogeneous file collections, built on Apache Tika with optional Tesseract OCR for scans and Redis-backed queueing to spread work across many machines.
journalism_use_case: Purpose-built for this domain — the tooling lineage ICIJ used to process multi-terabyte leaks, designed to chew through millions of mixed files, OCR the scanned ones at scale, and feed a search index.
deployment: local/self-hosted CLI; Redis for queueing; scales horizontally
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-13, archived=false, 257 stars; GitHub releases endpoint returns no release object — consumers must pin commits
external_deps: Apache Tika; Tesseract and Leptonica for OCR; Redis; typically Solr/Elasticsearch downstream
data_flows: fully self-hosted; designed for controlled leak handling
limitations: no tagged releases and a small user base outside ICIJ; engineer-operated with no UI; the OCR step is only as good as Tesseract

name: DocumentCloud
description: Back-end source for DocumentCloud, the newsroom document platform: upload, OCR, full-text search, annotate, embed and publish primary-source documents, extended by an open Add-On plugin system including swappable OCR add-ons.
journalism_use_case: Where processed documents go to become public evidence — searchable, annotatable and embeddable in a story. The Add-On model lets a newsroom choose its OCR engine and automate extraction and alerts.
deployment: primarily consumed as MuckRock's hosted service at documentcloud.org; source is available for self-hosting but that is a substantial undertaking
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-10, archived=false, 54 stars; no GitHub release objects. The related MuckRock/documentcloud-azure-document-intelligence-ocr-addon is BSD-3-Clause, pushed 2026-09-16
external_deps: Django stack, object storage, search index; OCR add-ons that can call Google Cloud Vision, Azure Document Intelligence or OCRSpace
data_flows: the hosted platform stores documents on MuckRock infrastructure, and the official high-accuracy OCR add-ons send pages to Google/Azure/OCRSpace APIs — both matter for unpublished or source-sensitive material
limitations: self-hosting is not a documented turnkey path; the best-performing OCR add-ons are third-party cloud APIs rather than local engines; small repo community

name: Paperless-ngx
description: Community-maintained document management system that ingests, OCRs, indexes, tags and archives documents with full-text search over the resulting archive.
journalism_use_case: Practical self-hosted archive for a moderate corpus of scanned or PDF source documents where reporters need tagging plus reliable OCR search without engineering support.
deployment: self-hosted Docker; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 48,159 stars; release v3.4.2 published 2026-11-03
external_deps: PostgreSQL/SQLite, Redis, Tesseract/OCRmyPDF toolchain
data_flows: fully local; no third-party calls required
limitations: architected around personal and office document volumes, not million-document leak triage; no clustering or topic discovery; GPL-3.0 affects redistribution

name: Apache Solr
description: Mature Lucene-based search server providing full-text search, faceting, highlighting and clustering over very large document sets.
journalism_use_case: Licence-clean index layer for a bespoke newsroom archive at multi-million-document scale, free of the Elastic licensing questions that come with the default Aleph/Datashare stack.
deployment: self-hosted; SolrCloud clustering; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-15, archived=false, 1,703 stars
external_deps: JVM; ZooKeeper for SolrCloud
data_flows: fully local/self-hosted
limitations: operational expertise needed for sharding and schema design; no reporter-facing UI without a front end such as Blacklight or a custom app

name: Datasette
description: Multi-tool for exploring and publishing data, exposing SQLite databases as a browsable, queryable web interface with full-text search via SQLite FTS and a large plugin ecosystem.
journalism_use_case: Fast way to give reporters a searchable, browsable view over extracted document text and metadata once a leak has been flattened into SQLite, and to publish a cleaned subset alongside a story.
deployment: local CLI, self-hosted, or one-command publish to cloud hosts; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16, archived=false, 11,578 stars
external_deps: SQLite; optional plugins such as datasette-search-all
data_flows: local by default, but the publish subcommands intentionally push data to third-party hosts — never run them against unvetted leak material
limitations: SQLite FTS is excellent for structured extracts but not a substitute for a sharded index over 2M full documents; read-only by design

name: BERTopic
description: Topic modelling technique that clusters transformer embeddings and derives interpretable topic descriptions via class-based TF-IDF, with hierarchical, dynamic and guided topic variants.
journalism_use_case: The strongest current answer to 'what themes are in this dump' — cluster a leak into human-readable topics and drill into each for reporting leads.
model_licence: varies by the chosen embedding model (not verified individually)
deployment: library, local; GPU recommended for large corpora
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-14, archived=false, 7,960 stars; release v0.17.4 published 2025-12-03
external_deps: sentence-transformers or another embedding backend, UMAP, HDBSCAN, scikit-learn
data_flows: local if a local embedding model is used; selecting an API-based embedding backend would send text to a third party
limitations: embedding millions of documents needs a GPU or substantial time; UMAP/HDBSCAN memory grows sharply at that scale, so sampling or incremental workflows are usually required; topic labels need human interpretation

name: datasketch
description: Probabilistic data structures for large-scale similarity search, including MinHash, MinHash LSH, LSH Forest, Weighted MinHash and HyperLogLog.
journalism_use_case: Deduplicating a leak at scale — collapsing thousands of near-identical email chains, attachment copies and boilerplate documents before reporters begin reading.
deployment: library, local; optional Redis/Cassandra-backed LSH storage; CPU only

name: txtai

model_licence: varies by the model selected (not verified individually)

name: sumy

journalism_use_case: Produces extractive, source-faithful summaries for rapid triage of long documents — safer than generative summarisation because every sentence is quoted verbatim from the original.

name: eyecite

name: Dangerzone
description: Converts potentially dangerous PDFs, office documents and images into safe PDFs by rendering them to raw pixel data inside a disposable container and rebuilding a clean document; offers an option to add an OCR text layer to the output.
journalism_use_case: The step before any other tool in this catalogue: a document from an unknown source is sanitised so opening it cannot execute an exploit or beacon out, protecting both the reporter and the source. Built by Freedom of the Press Foundation for exactly this threat model.
deployment: desktop app for macOS, Windows, Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Qubes OS and Tails; runs conversion inside a container runtime; CPU only
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-09, archived=false, 5,846 stars; release v0.11.1 published 2026-10-22
external_deps: container runtime (Docker/Podman); Tesseract for the optional OCR layer
data_flows: fully local — the whole premise is that nothing is uploaded and the conversion is isolated from the host
limitations: the pixel round-trip destroys the text layer unless OCR is enabled, and OCR'd text is then only as accurate as Tesseract; conversion is slow on large documents; container runtime dependency complicates locked-down machines
